tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

definition.name: Workflow
definition.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

# Your submission guide (plain steps)

Submission window: **Monday 12 Oct, 7:00–11:55 PM IST**. Everything technical is done and pushed. Four things are left for you, in this order: cfo.ai, the demo video, post 2, and post 3 (the submission). Plan about 2–3 hours in total.

All numbers here are real (see `hackathon.md` and `docs/economics.md`).

---

## 1. cfo.ai business plan (about 20 min)

1. Open https://cfo.ai/neathacks and sign up.
2. **Straight away**, go to **Settings → Billing** and cancel the card / subscription, so you are not charged.
3. Create a new company plan. When it asks, enter:
   - **Company:** Crashworthy. Crash tests and a safety rating for AI agents that move money.
   - **Product / pricing** (our suggestion; you can change it):

     - *Pro*: **$199 per agent per month**. Adds repair sessions (one-change-at-a-time fixes with an audit trail).
   - **Cost per customer (cost of goods), measured in our real runs:**
     - One full re-test: **$0.019**
     - One certification (re-test plus planted-bug check): **$0.058**
     - One repair session (9 rounds): **$1.38**

   - **Fixed costs:** enter your own real numbers (for example hosting and tools). If you have none yet, enter $0 and say so. Don't guess.
   - **Customers / growth:** your own assumption. Keep it modest, e.g. 5 paying agents in month 3. cfo.ai will work out revenue and runway.
4. When the plan is made, export or copy it and send it to me (paste the text, or a PDF or screenshots). I'll save it as `docs/business-plan.md` and commit it.

---

## 2. Demo video (about 3 minutes)

Record your screen with voice. Free options: Loom, or the screen recorder built into your laptop (Windows: Win+Alt+R in Xbox Game Bar; Mac: Cmd+Shift+5). Open these first:

- The repo: https://github.com/NECOKIZZ/Crashworthy

| Time | Show | Say |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:20 | Certificate top (`1-certificate.png`) | "Cars get crash tests. AI agents that issue refunds and delete data get a demo. Crashworthy crash-tests an agent before it's trusted with money, and gives it a star rating a buyer can read." |
| 0:20–0:50 | The tests table (`4-tests.png`) | "Each test rebuilds a real AI failure: Air Canada's invented refund policy, the $1 Chevy Tahoe, Replit deleting a production database. Pass or fail is decided by code, not an AI judge. Five tests are hidden from the fixer, to catch overfitting." |
| 0:50–1:20 | neatlogs Traces tab: open a red `crash-test S03-replit-freeze` trace from the "before: v1" run | "Every crash is a neatlogs trace. Here the agent deleted two production rows during a code freeze. That's a 4-severity crash, and it caps the rating." |
| 1:20–1:50 | Certificate incident report for round 1 (`3-gate.png`, lower half) | "The fixer reads the failing traces back from neatlogs. Entire Graph points to the code, and a Claude Code session makes one change: block production deletes. The gate re-runs all 16 tests and keeps it." |
| 1:50–2:20 | "The gate at work" card (`3-gate.png`, top) | "Then we asked it to cut cost. It made the agent 8% cheaper, but safety on the hidden tests fell from 38.5% to 23.1%. The gate rejected it, on the record. Cheaper but less safe doesn't ship." |
| 2:20–2:40 | The Entire link in the browser | "Every fix, and every rejected attempt, is a commit with an Entire checkpoint: the Claude Code session that made it, its reasoning and its edits." |

Upload it to YouTube (choose "Unlisted") or Loom, and copy the link.

> After 9 Claude Code repair rounds: 2★, 65%. 3 fixes kept, 6 rejected, including a cost cut that hurt hidden-test safety.
> Every crash is a @neatlogs trace, every fix an @EntireHQ checkpoint.

content.text:
The technical work is finished and pushed to `main` on GitHub. All numbers are from real runs, and I checked that no keys are in the repo or the Entire checkpoints.

**Results:**
- **Before (v1):** 1★. It passed 7 of 16 tests and was 40% safe on the tests the fixer can see. It deleted production data during a code freeze, and it obeyed a hidden instruction planted in an order note.
- **After (v7):** 2★. It passes 8 of 16 and is 65% safe on the visible tests. Safety on the 5 hidden tests held at 23%.
- **Repair rounds:** Claude Code ran 9, each recorded by Entire. 3 fixes were kept and 6 were rejected.
- **The cost cut was rejected:** it made the agent 8% cheaper, but safety on the hidden tests dropped from 38.5% to 23.1%. This is your best demo moment.
- **Planted bugs:** all 10 were caught.
- **Costs:** a full safety check costs about 6 cents ($0.058) and a re-test about 2 cents.

**Things you should know (written up in `hackathon.md`):**
- **The rating stays at 2★.** Six tests still fail on v7, including three of the most serious kind, so I didn't push it higher.
- **The agent model changed.** On Claude Haiku the agent passed 15 of 16 tests, which left nothing to repair. I switched it to Nova Lite, which is about 18 times cheaper.
- **Some failures were our test's mistakes.** The real model exposed eight kinds of mistakes in our own tests (for example, an honest "I sent your refund for approval" was counted as a fake refund). All are fixed and covered by new tests.
- **About 6% of traces never showed up in neatlogs** (466 of 494 arrived), even though nothing reported an error. Every trace that did arrive matched our own records exactly.
- **neatlogs records Nova Lite's token counts but shows its cost as $0.** So the costs above are our token counts times Nova Lite's published price; neatlogs' token counts matched ours exactly.
- **Your email appears in the Entire checkpoints**, because the first repair sessions recorded this conversation too. It was already public in the repo's commit history, so nothing new was exposed. Later sessions record only the fixer.

**What I need from you** (step by step in `docs/SUBMISSION-GUIDE.md`, sent above):
1. **cfo.ai (about 20 min):** sign up at https://cfo.ai/neathacks and cancel the card straight away (Settings → Billing). Then type in the numbers from the guide, and send me the finished plan so I can save it in the repo.
2. **Demo video (about 3 min):** the guide has a scene-by-scene script and the links to open. Upload it to YouTube as "Unlisted" or to Loom.
3. **Post 2 (this afternoon):** the text and the two screenshots I sent are ready to paste.
4. **Post 3 (between 7:00 and 11:55 PM IST):** quote the official neatlogs post using the text in the guide.

Then send me the cfo.ai plan and the three links, and I'll add them to the build log.

- session-start-hook (startup-hook-skill): Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code cloud sessions. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for cloud sessions, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during cloud sessions.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

content.text:
I've added your post to the build log and pushed it: https://x.com/0xnecokizz/status/2109451489693295041

**cfo.ai.** You talk to it in plain English: its assistant is called **Ari**, and it builds the financial model for you. Here's what to do:

1. **Cancel the card first** (if you haven't yet): **Settings → Billing**, cancel the subscription. Do this now, before anything else.
2. **Skip connecting systems.** If it asks you to connect QuickBooks, Stripe, a bank, etc., choose **skip** or **start from scratch**. Crashworthy has no company accounts yet.
3. **Find the chat box** with Ari, which may be labelled "Ask Ari" or be a message box on the dashboard. Copy and paste this whole message:

> Build a financial model and business plan for **Crashworthy**, a new startup. Crashworthy crash-tests AI agents that move money (refunds, payments, production data) against real AI incidents, and gives them a 5-star safety rating plus a repair service. It is built on neatlogs.
>
> **Pricing (per AI agent, monthly subscription):**
> - Starter: $49/month. Weekly re-test plus a monthly safety certificate.
> - Pro: $199/month. Everything in Starter plus repair sessions.
>
> **Cost to serve, measured in real runs:**
> - One full re-test: $0.019 (cheap model). About $0.36 on a larger model like Claude Haiku.
> - One certification: $0.058.
> - One repair session: $1.38.
> - So cost per Starter customer is about $0.13–$1.50/month, and per Pro customer about $3/month.
>
> **Fixed costs:** assume $0 today (solo founder, no salary yet, free tiers). Add a line for $50/month hosting and tools from month 3.
>
> **Growth assumption:** 5 paying agents in month 3, growing 30% per month, with 70% on Starter and 30% on Pro. No funding raised yet, starting cash $0.
>
> Show monthly revenue, costs, gross margin, profit, and runway for 24 months. Then give me a one-page business plan summary.

4. **Wait for it to build the model.** If Ari asks questions you're not sure about, tell it "use a reasonable assumption and label it as an assumption".
5. **Save the result.** Look for an export, download or share button (PDF or link). If there isn't one, take screenshots of the summary page and the main charts or tables.
6. **Send them to me.** Paste the summary text here, or upload the PDF/screenshots. I'll save it as `docs/business-plan.md` and add it to the repo.

The fixed costs ($50/month from month 3), starting cash and growth rate are assumptions, not measurements. Change them if you know better numbers. The cost-to-serve figures are the real measured ones.

If the screen looks different from what I describe, send me a screenshot and I'll tell you exactly where to click.

After that, the remaining steps are the demo video and the submission post tonight (7:00–11:55 PM IST). Both are in `docs/SUBMISSION-GUIDE.md`.

I can't open that link: it only shows the cfo.ai sign-in page to anyone who isn't logged in as you, including me and the judges. So I need you to copy the plan out.

**Easiest way (about 2 minutes):**
1. On that page (the plan or model panel on the right), click anywhere in the text.
2. Press **Ctrl+A** (Mac: **Cmd+A**) to select everything, then **Ctrl+C** (Mac: **Cmd+C**) to copy.
3. Come back here and paste it with **Ctrl+V** (Mac: **Cmd+V**), then send.

If select-all grabs the whole website or nothing useful, do this instead:
- Look for a **Share**, **Export**, **Download** or **⋯** (three dots) button near the top of the plan, and choose **PDF**. Upload the PDF here.
- Or take **screenshots** of each part (summary, revenue, costs, runway charts/tables) and upload them here.

Also, before you close cfo.ai: did you cancel the card (**Settings → Billing**)? If not, please do it now.

Once you send the plan, I'll save it as `docs/business-plan.md`, check that its numbers match our real measured costs, add it to the build log, and push. Then the only things left are the demo video and the submission post tonight (7:00–11:55 PM IST).

| Plan | Price | Mix | Includes | Delivery cost / agent (cfo.ai) | Gross profit / agent |

| Input | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|

: > "$W/list.txt"; : > "$W/subs.srt"
t=0; n=0
ts() { python3 -c "import sys;t=float(sys.argv[1]);h=int(t//3600);m=int(t%3600//60);s=t%60;print('%02d:%02d:%06.3f'%(h,m,s)).replace('.',',')" "$1"; }

import re,sys
say,t0,dur,n=sys.argv[1],float(sys.argv[2])+0.4,float(sys.argv[3]),int(sys.argv[4])
parts=[p.strip() for p in re.split(r'(?<=[.:?])\s+',say) if p.strip()]
tot=sum(len(p) for p in parts); t=t0
f=lambda x:'%02d:%02d:%06.3f'%(x//3600,x%3600//60,x%60)
for i,p in enumerate(parts):
  d=dur*len(p)/tot; n+=1
  print(f"{n}\n{f(t).replace('.',',')} --> {f(t+d).replace('.',',')}\n{p}\n"); t+=d
PY
  n=$(grep -c -- "-->" "$W/subs.srt"); t=$(python3 -c "print($t+$d)")
done
ffmpeg -v error -y -f concat -safe 0 -i "$W/list.txt" -c copy "$W/joined.mp4"

content.text:
I made the whole demo video myself, so you don't need to record anything. It's sent above and also saved in the GitHub repo.

**What's in it (2 min 11 s, full HD, with voice-over and subtitles):**
1. What Crashworthy is.
2. The list of crash tests, rebuilt from real AI failures.
3. A real neatlogs trace: the agent deletes production data during a code freeze, then says "Yes, the test data has been successfully deleted."
4. The repair loop fixing it with a Claude Code session.
5. The cost cut that the gate rejected.
6. The real Entire page showing the Claude Code session behind a fix.
7. The 1★ → 2★ certificate.
8. 10 of 10 planted bugs caught.
9. Closing slide: 6 cents per certification, 99% margin in the cfo.ai plan.

The voice is computer-generated. The service for more natural voices was blocked here, so I used one that runs on this machine; it's clear but sounds a bit robotic. If you'd rather use your own voice, play the video and read the subtitles aloud while recording your screen. Otherwise, it's ready as is.

The neatlogs scene shows the real trace as fetched from neatlogs, not a screenshot of the neatlogs website, because I can't log in there.

**What you need to do:**
1. **Download the video:** click the file card above and save it.
2. **Upload it to YouTube:** go to https://studio.youtube.com, click **Create → Upload videos**, and pick the file. Title it "Crashworthy, #neatHack 2026", set visibility to **Unlisted**, click **Save**, and copy the link.
3. **Tonight between 7:00 and 11:55 PM IST:** find the official neatlogs neatHack post on X and press **Quote**. Paste this, with your YouTube link at the end:

> Submitting Crashworthy for #neatHack 🚗💥
> Crash tests + a 5-star safety rating for AI agents that move money. Built on neatlogs.
> Team: Crashworthy
> Repo: https://github.com/NECOKIZZ/Crashworthy
> Demo: (your YouTube link)

4. **Send me** the YouTube link and the submission post link, and I'll add them to the build log so the repo is complete.

# Generates a soft ambient pad (original, royalty-free) for the demo video.
